input.strategy_title: Adopt structured JSON logging across RHOAI components
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

RHOAI components log in inconsistent formats — plain text, key=value, and
ad-hoc JSON — which breaks centralized log queries and makes support cases
expensive: correlating one user request across Dashboard, serving, and
pipelines requires per-component parsing rules. The platform needs one
structured logging convention, and each component needs to adopt it. Component
adoptions are independent of each other once the convention exists.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1  | P0 | A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema, required fields (timestamp, level, component, namespace, correlation id), and library guidance per language (Go, Python, TypeScript). |
| HLR-2  | P0 | Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-3  | P0 | KServe controller and serving runtimes emit convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-4  | P1 | Data Science Pipelines (operator and API server) emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-5  | P1 | Model Registry emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-6  | P1 | TrustyAI services emit convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-7  | P1 | Notebooks (notebook-controller) emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-8  | P2 | Training Operator emits convention-conformant logs. |
| HLR-9  | P2 | Documentation describes the log format and example queries for common support scenarios. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- KServe
- Data Science Pipelines
- Model Registry
- TrustyAI
- Notebooks
- Training Operator

## Out of Scope

- Log storage, retention, or forwarding infrastructure
- Metrics and tracing conventions (logging only)

## Open Questions

None — the convention work (HLR-1) is prerequisite design, and per-component
adoptions are mechanical once it lands.

# Publish platform structured JSON logging convention

## Description

This epic delivers the platform-wide structured logging convention that all
RHOAI component logging adoptions build against: a JSON log-record schema with
required fields, and per-language library guidance so that component teams
produce conformant output without re-inventing the design. It is the
prerequisite design work for every per-component adoption in the strategy.

## Scope

- Define the JSON log-record schema: valid JSON per log line, with required
  fields `timestamp`, `level`, `component`, `namespace`, and `correlation id`.
- Provide library guidance for each language used by affected components —
  Go, Python, and TypeScript: which structured logging approach to use and
  how to emit records that validate against the schema.
- Define how the correlation id is populated so a single user request can be
  correlated across components (Dashboard, serving, pipelines) without
  per-component parsing rules.
- Publish the convention where adopting teams can reference it, and obtain
  review/sign-off from the owning teams of the adopting components.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A published convention document defines the JSON log-record schema, and the
  schema requires the fields `timestamp`, `level`, `component`, `namespace`,
  and `correlation id`.
- A sample record validating against the schema can be produced for each of
  Go, Python, and TypeScript using the documented library guidance.
- The convention defines correlation-id population rules sufficient to
  correlate one user request across Dashboard, serving, and pipelines.
- The convention is reviewed and acknowledged by the owning teams of the
  components listed in the strategy's affected components (Dashboard, KServe,
  Data Science Pipelines, Model Registry, TrustyAI, Notebooks, Training
  Operator, plus the serving runtimes).
- Out of scope is respected: no log storage, retention, forwarding, metrics,
  or tracing conventions are introduced.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A platform logging convention is published: JSON schema,
  required fields, and library guidance per language.

# Adopt structured JSON logging in Dashboard

## Description

Convert the Dashboard (odh-dashboard, TypeScript) to emit logs conformant to
the published platform structured JSON logging convention, so Dashboard log
lines can be queried centrally alongside other components and correlated with
serving and pipelines activity by correlation id.

## Scope

- Replace existing Dashboard logging (plain text / ad-hoc formats) with
  structured JSON output that validates against the platform log-record
  schema, including the required fields timestamp, level, component,
  namespace, and correlation id.
- Follow the TypeScript library guidance from the platform convention.
- Propagate the correlation id on user-initiated operations where the
  Dashboard is the entry point, so downstream serving and pipelines log lines
  can be correlated back to the originating request.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All Dashboard log output is valid JSON per the platform convention schema,
  with all required fields present.
- A support-style query on the required fields (e.g., by correlation id)
  returns Dashboard log lines for a user request without component-specific
  parsing rules.
- The change is rollback-safe: a documented revert or gating path exists so
  support tooling relying on the previous format is not broken unrecoverably.
- The Dashboard build pipeline remains green.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Dashboard emits convention-conformant logs.

# Adopt structured JSON logging in serving runtimes

## Description

Convert the serving runtimes (model-execution runtimes such as vLLM, OpenVINO,
and Caikit used by KServe for model serving) to emit logs conformant to the
published platform structured JSON logging convention, so model-serving
runtime log lines can be queried centrally and correlated with inference
requests.

## Scope

- Update logging in each serving runtime (or its launch configuration, where
  the runtime's own logger can be configured to conformant output) so emitted
  records validate against the platform log-record schema, including the
  required fields timestamp, level, component, namespace, and correlation id.
- Apply the language-appropriate library guidance from the platform convention
  for each runtime's stack.
- Carry the correlation id through to runtime log lines where the inference
  request context provides one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each serving runtime in the platform emits valid JSON per the platform
  convention schema, with all required fields present.
- Runtime log lines are queryable by correlation id without per-runtime
  parsing rules.
- The change is rollback-safe: a documented revert or gating path exists so
  support tooling relying on the previous format is not broken unrecoverably.
- Build pipelines for affected runtime images remain green.

## HLR Traceability

  convention-conformant logs (serving runtimes portion).
